meta.method: Every quote was matched by script against the plain text named in its locator (whitespace normalised, OCR line-end hyphens joined; OCR misreadings normalised only where a quote_note says so). Every outdoor point was checked by script against the 1812 footprints (1 m clear of any roofed building and of the picket lines) and against the 1812 river polygon, and no two of these women stand within 1 m of each other at the same time. Points within the soldiers' stations of place.py were avoided by hand.
meta.times: Hours are local solar time, 0-24. Reveille 5:30 and tattoo 21:00 as place.py. Dinner is the noon meal.
meta.dates: Each person has a presence range and "days" by date range: a plain summer day up to 13 August (and, for the Kinzie women and the two settler wives, a separate plain day before the 6/7 April alarm), the 14 August day, and for those still in town after the battle a day for 16-18 August (Kinzie household) or the rest of 1812 (Ouilmette household). 15 August is the battle jaunt's and is not planned here.
meta.jaunts: Stops that name these women: battle-of-fort-dearborn the-fort (6 Apr; Helm/Kinzie/Burns/Ouilmette/Lee households), burns (6 Apr: Mrs. Burns brought out on her bed), the-gate (14 Aug sunset: Wells, Rebekah Heald's uncle), the-bank (Cicely), ouilmette (16 Aug: Margaret Helm, Mrs. Bisson); first-fort-dearborn-tour commandant and officers (14 Aug: Rebekah Heald, Margaret Helm, battledore); killing-of-jean-lalime the-flight (17 June: the family account has Kinzie go home and his wife hide him in the woods).
meta.liberty: Almost every span is reconstructed: where each woman stood and when is ours, built from the period routine of a garrison and a trader's household and bent by the day's recorded events. Suggested liberty id L-1812-women-day-3464.

conflicts_and_owner_questions.detail: The household card hh_kinzie_john_elder keeps the family at kinzie_house_1812 from 1804 with no change; Quaife and Wau-Bun put the family inside the fort from the April alarm. Here: the fort, from 7 April. Which quarters is not recorded; reconstructed as Lieutenant Helm's, the officers' barracks (son-in-law). Owner may prefer the north range or a tent on the parade.

The Kinzie family tradition (Gordon 1912: "staggered home"; the Lalime jaunt's the-flight) puts Eleanor at the Kinzie house that night, which conflicts with the family living in the fort since April. Not resolved; the plain fort day stands for June.
Wau-Bun dates the Lee's Place murders 7 April, Quaife 6 April; the battle jaunt uses 6 April. The move into the fort is put on 7 April (the morning after, at latest).
Heald's report: 13 August; Helm: 12th; Wau-Bun: 14th. The battle jaunt's the-gate has him ride in at sunset on the 14th; these days follow Heald and have him at dinner on the 14th.
The card's first_fort_dearborn_small_house_sw is 5.5 x 7.7 ft on the draught, too small to sleep a family. Followed; a barracks room would be more believable.
dress.json says no portrait of her was found; garrison.json (and this file) record the Quaife 1913 daguerreotype plate and the Kirkland 1893 engraving, both public domain in print.
dress.json says about 43; Gordon 1912 makes her eight in autumn 1779, so about 41. Kirkland gives the marriage as 1800, Gordon 23 January 1798.

Quaife says "all of the other residents" fortified the agency house after the April murders, which would include the Ouilmettes; Currey and the Head Papers keep the household at its own house in August. Here: their own house all year.
